payload.source_label: Hyperbolic equations with variable coefficients may not be in conservation form

contract.statement: Within the book's first-order hyperbolic setting, equations with variable coefficients need not be in conservation form. The selected clause asserts this possibility without specifying a counterexample or a criterion excluding all alternative representations. Conservation form is contextualized by the flux PDE (1.8) and the interval balance (1.10). [Raw PDF page 30, printed page 8, second paragraph, opening clause; raw PDF page 25, printed page 3, first-order scope and equation (1.8); raw PDF page 26, printed page 4, equation (1.10).]
assumptions: The equations under discussion are hyperbolic and have variable coefficients. These are class qualifiers in the selected sentence, rather than a displayed list of theorem hypotheses. [Raw PDF page 30, printed page 8, selected opening clause.]
The book restricts its discussion to first-order hyperbolic systems. [Raw PDF page 25, printed page 3, paragraph following equation (1.7).]
Spatially varying material properties, including discontinuities in the medium, motivate the surrounding variable-coefficient discussion. [Raw PDF page 30, printed page 8, first paragraph.]
Constant-coefficient linear systems provide a contrasting established conservation-form case with flux f(q) = Aq. [Raw PDF pages 25–26, printed pages 3–4, sentence spanning the page boundary.]
quantifiers: The selected clause concerns the class of hyperbolic equations with variable coefficients; it supplies no explicit symbolic binders, coefficient functions, dimensions, or domains. [Raw PDF page 30, printed page 8, second paragraph, opening clause.]
